acceptance_criteria: AC1 — One shared AuditableAggregateRoot; no soft-delete-specific hierarchy
AC2 — Seven in-scope aggregates migrated without duplicate implementations
AC3 — MediaAsset, RefreshSession, and CatalogTerm models/schemas unchanged
AC4 — Immutable audit view and correct protected touch behavior
AC5 — Strict first/second soft-delete metadata semantics
AC6 — Existing important errors and observable behavior preserved
AC7 — exclude/include/only options with exclude default
AC8 — TypeORM find and query-builder semantics for all three modes
AC9 — Every in-scope aggregate read, count, and custom query propagates mode
AC10 — findByIdIncludingDeleted removed and callers migrated
AC11 — Default/include/only row and count behavior
AC12 — Six-field audit mapper helpers and migrated mappers
AC14 — No TypeORM, request context, or clock leakage into domain abstraction
AC15 — No HTTP API, schema, migration, or unrelated behavior change
AC16 — Required base, mode, mapper, exists, paginated-list, and cascade tests
AC17 — lint, typecheck, test, architecture test, and build pass
AC18 — Complete and accurate final handoff/evidence inventory

risk_areas.evidence: Mapped AC1-AC18 from task.md; context.lock lists no unconsolidated addendum.
Reviewed touch, first/second soft delete, aggregate-specific error overrides, status/token behavior, and seven migrated aggregates.
Reviewed every changed repository read, TypeORM helper, query-builder/raw SQL path, list total, join behavior, and facet-count branch.
CodeGraph traced ports, adapters, modules, use cases, and callers; deterministic checks passed 32 port bindings and 39 wired classes.
Transaction-aware repository resolution remains unchanged; account cascade and rollback paths were inspected. Real e2e execution evidence is missing and reported.

risk_areas.area: Security, authorization, injection, and sensitive data
risk_areas.evidence: No HTTP/auth boundary changed. Every deletedRecordWhereSql consumer passes a repository-owned literal alias; no request input reaches SQL interpolation and no secrets/PII logging was added.
No DTO, controller, HTTP contract, entity column, schema, or migration changed; build/typecheck/architecture evidence passed.
All ten repository implementations and five concrete test callers plus mocks were inventoried; remaining .delete calls are unrelated TypeORM/collection/HTTP APIs.
Inspected all new/changed tests and current summary/provenance. Five configured commands passed, but nested Date, facet-mode, and real-database cases remain unresolved.

test_contract.scenario: Inventory all AggregateRoot subclasses after introducing the shared auditable base.
test_contract.expected_result: Exactly the seven in-scope aggregates use AuditableAggregateRoot; CatalogTerm, MediaAsset, and RefreshSession retain AggregateRoot.

test_contract.scenario: A caller mutates a Date obtained from aggregate.audit.
test_contract.expected_result: The aggregate's internal createdAt/updatedAt/deletedAt values remain unchanged.

test_contract.scenario: A subclass mutation invokes touch with a new actor and time.
test_contract.expected_result: Only updatedBy and updatedAt change; creation metadata remains unchanged.

test_contract.scenario: Soft-delete an active aggregate once.
test_contract.expected_result: Delete and update metadata use the same actor/time and isDeleted becomes true.

test_contract.target: Strict repeated soft delete and observable errors
test_contract.scenario: Soft-delete an already deleted aggregate.
test_contract.expected_result: A conflict is raised without overwriting original metadata; existing Account/UserProfile codes are preserved.

test_contract.scenario: Translate exclude, include, and only for TypeORM find conditions and SQL aliases.
test_contract.expected_result: IsNull, no condition/1=1, and Not(IsNull)/IS NOT NULL are produced respectively.

sources: diff-impact: seven TypeORM repository find/business-key/exists/list implementations
test_contract.scenario: Use omitted, include, and only options across findById, business-key lookup, exists, findAll, list, and total.
test_contract.expected_result: Every standard read consistently applies the selected main-aggregate mode.

test_contract.scenario: Run paginated list under each deleted mode.
test_contract.expected_result: Items and total/count share the same deleted predicate.

test_contract.scenario: Request include or only semantics for facet/count reads.
test_contract.expected_result: All main-aggregate facet counts honor the requested mode.

sources: diff-impact: TypeOrmAccountRepository#list joins and catalog-term facet/list joins
test_contract.scenario: Change the main aggregate deleted mode on a joined query.
test_contract.expected_result: Only the main aggregate mode changes; existing joined-record active/deleted semantics remain intact.

test_contract.scenario: Inventory findByIdIncludingDeleted definitions and callers.
test_contract.expected_result: No executable reference remains; callers use findById(..., {deleted:'include'}).

test_contract.scenario: Round-trip all six audit fields with null and non-null actors and deleted timestamps.
test_contract.expected_result: All values and nullability are preserved without bounded-context coupling.

sources: diff-impact: Repository#hardDelete and ten TypeORM implementations
test_contract.scenario: Inventory implementations, application callers, cleanup callers, and mocks after rename.
test_contract.expected_result: Physical semantics remain unchanged and no domain repository delete method/caller is missed.

sources: diff-impact: DeleteAccountUseCase#execute and inherited strict softDelete
test_contract.scenario: Delete an account with active and already-deleted identities, then exercise not-found and repeated-delete paths.
test_contract.expected_result: Active records cascade once, already-deleted identities are skipped, and failures do not execute later side effects.

sources: requirement: transaction regression and locked definition-of-done
test_contract.scenario: Execute the account transaction rollback test against real PostgreSQL and supporting services.
test_contract.expected_result: No active or deleted account/identity/profile/role row survives rollback.

test_contract.scenario: Trace every alias supplied to the interpolating SQL helper.
test_contract.expected_result: Every alias is implementation-controlled and no request value reaches interpolation.

sources: diff-impact: public exports, repository interfaces, ORM adapters
test_contract.scenario: Compile and build after internal contract changes without modifying HTTP DTOs, entities, or migrations.
test_contract.expected_result: No HTTP or schema change occurs and architectural boundaries remain valid.

initial_findings.title: The read-only audit snapshot still exposes mutable Date references
initial_findings.expected_fix: Make every timestamp exposed by audit independent from internal mutable state and add regression coverage for Date mutation.
